comments.author: @mariokotlar303
comments.text: You were hitting rate limits, but you haven't mentioned which tier API you are using?  Claude 3.5 Sonnet which this is running on has a tier 1 rate limit of 40k tokens per minute. Best case you were hitting this, but even then it implies that "computer use" is burning more than 40k tokens per minute. 1M input tokens costs $3, 1M output costs 15$. This comes out to  between $0.12 and $0.6 per minute of usage while hitting the rate limit, so in reality it's somewhat more than that. If we assume 50-50% input output that's slightly more than $0.36 per minute of usage,  so probably $0.5, assuming you have tier 1. If you have tier 2, it's double that much, and if tier 3, then double that much again. But even assuming tier 1, this seems expensive, like it would cost potentially up to $5 for 15 minutes? Unless input output token distribution is very skewed.

comments.author: @jantuitman
comments.text: I think this is dumb. Why: if you went to live in a new home together with another human you don’t really know well, you’d never give this human the same access to your computer as you have. What are we doing here? Instead of releasing an agentic framework where we humans can choose what can be automated, they release software that allows the AI full access to screen and keyboard as if it has our own credentials. Sure it saves Anthropic some time: they don’t have build new interfaces for the automations but can reuse the existing remote desktop like api’s to give Claude access. But it is setting up the world for future security bugs, both by evil humans (get access to anyone’s desktop by prompt injection) and by malfunctioning AIs or by AIs that are not aligned with your own goals.
